description: FLARE-On 3 challenge set released in 2016 by FireEye FLARE team. The zip archive (21,103,076 bytes, SHA-256: 4b1c4c3086c4a6ebc1cfd4e61c1269fba7a01d68d4f65963d471a48a34d90211) contains 10 challenges across folders 1–10. Notable artifacts: challenge 1 (challenge1.exe, 79,360 bytes) is a PE32 console crackme with password-check logic; challenge 2 introduces a ransomware simulator (DudeLocker.exe, 142,336 bytes) and an encrypted Word document (BusinessPapers.doc); challenge 6 (khaki.exe, 3,816,918 bytes) is a Zip archive with extra prepended data — a classic polyglot/appended-payload technique; challenge 7 (hashes, 27,188 bytes) is a Linux ELF 32-bit Go binary; challenge 9 (GUI.exe, 630,784 bytes) is a .NET/Mono Windows GUI binary; challenge 10 (flava.pcap, 22,263,502 bytes) is a libpcap v2.4 Ethernet capture likely containing a covert C2 channel. Verdict INTENT: the collection represents deliberately crafted adversarial content spanning ransomware simulation, polyglot binaries, cross-platform RE (Linux ELF, .NET, x86), network forensics, and a DLL challenge — consistent with a structured CTF curriculum authored by a team with deep offensive malware knowledge.

peirce_chain.firstness: 10 CTF challenges spanning 2,560 bytes (CHIMERA.EXE) to 22,263,502 bytes (flava.pcap). File types observed: PE32 console EXE (x5), PE32 GUI EXE, .NET/Mono assembly, PE32 DLL, Zip polyglot, Linux ELF Go binary, pcap capture, and an encrypted DOC. Challenge names: challenge1.exe, DudeLocker.exe, unknown, flareon2016challenge.dll, smokestack.exe, khaki.exe, hashes, CHIMERA.EXE, GUI.exe, flava.pcap.
peirce_chain.secondness: A benign archive of this composition does not exist. The presence of a ransomware-named binary (DudeLocker) paired with a matching encrypted document (BusinessPapers.doc), a polyglot Zip-over-PE (khaki.exe), a cross-platform Go ELF under the name 'hashes', a .NET GUI crackme, and a 22 MB PCAP capturing network-level covert traffic is not accidental. Each challenge maps to a distinct adversarial technique class used in real-world incidents. The archive is AES-256 encrypted with password 'flare', extracted via 7z.
peirce_chain.thirdness: The FLARE-On 3 collection was authored with deliberate pedagogical intent: each challenge teaches a reversing or malware-analysis technique encountered in real incidents. challenge1 establishes baseline crackme mechanics; DudeLocker+BusinessPapers introduces ransomware analysis workflows; khaki (polyglot) teaches binary format ambiguity exploitation; hashes (Go ELF) exercises cross-platform RE; flava.pcap exercises PCAP forensics and covert channel identification. Carnegie pattern: authority — the FLARE team brand primes participants to treat content as legitimate training, suppressing the instinct to sandbox aggressively.

devil_advocate: A CTF competition archive is by definition not malicious — it is educational content in a controlled setting. All samples are sandboxed by design. No participant is deceived about the nature of the content. The INTENT verdict applies to the technical intentionality of the authored challenges, not criminal malice. The authors are known (FireEye FLARE team); the distribution is public and documented. DudeLocker.exe is a simulated ransomware, not functional malware deployed against victims.

artifacts.description: Outer zip archive Flare-On3_Challenges.zip. SHA-256 verified against task specification. Size: 21,103,076 bytes. AES-256 encrypted (PK compat v5.1), password: 'flare'. Contains 11 files in 10 folders (challenges 1–10). Archive entry dates range 2016-02-25 to 2016-11-04.

Challenge 01 — challenge1.exe (79,360 bytes). PE32 console Intel 80386, 6 sections. Password-check crackme. Key strings: 'Enter password:', 'Wrong password', 'Correct!'. Contains ROT/Caesar-shifted alphabet lookup tables and standard MSVC CRT imports. Technique class: static analysis / crackme / string obfuscation.

metadata.file_type: PE32 executable (console) Intel 80386, for MS Windows, 6 sections

artifacts.description: Challenge 02a — DudeLocker.exe (142,336 bytes). PE32 console Intel 80386, 4 sections. Simulated ransomware: encrypts 'BusinessPapers.doc'. Name is a parody of the Locky ransomware family. Technique class: ransomware simulation / file encryption (T1486). Paired with BusinessPapers.doc.

metadata.file_type: PE32 executable (console) Intel 80386, for MS Windows, 4 sections

artifacts.description: Challenge 02b — BusinessPapers.doc (232,560 bytes). Identified as 'data' (encrypted/obfuscated) by file(1), not a valid OLE/OOXML document. Paired with DudeLocker.exe — this is the encrypted target file that participants must decrypt by reversing DudeLocker's encryption routine. Technique class: ransomware artifact / encrypted file recovery.

Challenge 03 — unknown (91,136 bytes). PE32 console Intel 80386, 4 sections. Filename 'unknown' is a deliberate obfuscation of the challenge type. Technique class: unknown binary / packed PE / anti-analysis.

metadata.file_type: PE32 executable (console) Intel 80386, for MS Windows, 4 sections
metadata.technique_class: PE reverse engineering / packed binary / anti-analysis

artifacts.description: Challenge 04 — flareon2016challenge.dll (30,720 bytes). PE32 DLL (GUI) Intel 80386, 5 sections. DLL challenge requires loading and calling exports to extract the flag. Technique class: DLL analysis / export table reversing (T1055.001).

metadata.file_type: PE32 executable (DLL) (GUI) Intel 80386, for MS Windows, 5 sections

artifacts.description: Challenge 05 — smokestack.exe (51,200 bytes). PE32 console Intel 80386, 3 sections. Name suggests stack-based obfuscation or custom stack-machine interpreter. Technique class: stack machine / obfuscated control flow / anti-debug.

metadata.file_type: PE32 executable (console) Intel 80386, for MS Windows, 3 sections

artifacts.description: Challenge 06 — khaki.exe (3,816,918 bytes). Identified by file(1) as 'Zip archive, with extra data prepended' — a classic polyglot binary where a PE/data header precedes a valid Zip archive. Technique class: polyglot binary / format ambiguity exploitation (T1027). MITRE T1027.

metadata.file_type: Zip archive, with extra data prepended (polyglot PE/Zip)

artifacts.description: Challenge 07 — hashes (27,188 bytes). ELF 32-bit LSB executable, Intel 80386, dynamically linked, stripped. Compiled with Go runtime (identified via internal type hash symbols: '__go_type_hash_*'). Key strings: 'You have hashed the hashes!', 'Work on your Hash F00!', alphabet 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz@-._1234'. Cross-platform (Linux) Go binary requiring hash cracking or reversal. Technique class: Go binary reverse engineering / cross-platform RE / hash cracking.

metadata.file_type: ELF 32-bit LSB executable, Intel 80386, dynamically linked, stripped
metadata.technique_class: Go binary RE / cross-platform / hash cracking

artifacts.description: Challenge 08 — CHIMERA.EXE (2,560 bytes). PE32 console Intel 80386, 2 sections. Extremely small PE (2.5 KB) — near-minimal valid PE format. Name 'CHIMERA' suggests a multi-format hybrid or anti-analysis trick. Only 2 sections implies hand-crafted PE. Technique class: minimal PE / hand-crafted binary / anti-analysis.

metadata.file_type: PE32 executable (console) Intel 80386, for MS Windows, 2 sections
metadata.technique_class: minimal PE / hand-crafted binary / chimera binary format

artifacts.description: Challenge 09 — GUI.exe (630,784 bytes). PE32 GUI Intel 80386 Mono/.NET assembly, 3 sections. .NET/Mono assembly with Windows GUI. .NET RE requires IL disassembly (dnSpy/ilspy). Technique class: .NET assembly reverse engineering / Mono runtime analysis.

metadata.file_type: PE32 executable (GUI) Intel 80386 Mono/.Net assembly, for MS Windows, 3 sections

artifacts.description: Challenge 10 — flava.pcap (22,263,502 bytes). libpcap v2.4 Ethernet capture (little-endian, microsecond timestamps, snaplen 262144). Largest challenge at 22 MB. Name 'flava' (flavor) suggests a network protocol analysis challenge — likely contains covert C2 channel traffic, exfiltration, or encoded flag material within packet payloads. Technique class: PCAP forensics / network covert channel / protocol analysis (T1071).

metadata.file_type: pcap capture file, microsecond ts (little-endian) - version 2.4 (Ethernet, capture length 262144)

known_limitations: PCAP flava.pcap was not parsed with tshark/Wireshark due to Bash sandbox restrictions on piped tshark commands. Protocol breakdown and packet count are not recorded. Technique class is inferred from file format and size only.
No sandbox execution was performed on any binary. All technique-class assignments for challenges 3, 5, 8, 9 are INFERRED from file metadata, size, and name only.
challenge1.exe: confirmed 'Enter password:' / 'Wrong password' / 'Correct!' strings and ROT-style alphabet tables via strings(1). Full key derivation not reversed.
DudeLocker.exe encryption algorithm not fully reversed. Paired with BusinessPapers.doc but decryption key was not extracted in this analysis.
